```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper functions (adapted from 03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ct_to_label <- function(ct) tolower(gsub("_", "", ct))

comp_label <- function(comp) {
  switch(toupper(comp), C2 = "NMD", C4 = "Control", toupper(comp))
}

evt_types <- c("Alt_TSS", "Alt_TES", "A5SS", "A3SS", "SE",
               "Missing_Internal", "IR", "IR_diff",
               "Partial_IR_5", "Partial_IR_3")

compute_event_freq <- function(profiles) {
  n_pairs <- nrow(profiles)
  n_pir5 <- sum(sapply(profiles$detailed_events, function(de)
    any(de$event_type == "Partial_IR_5")))
  n_pir3 <- sum(sapply(profiles$detailed_events, function(de)
    any(de$event_type == "Partial_IR_3")))
  counts <- c(sum(profiles$tss_changed), sum(profiles$tes_changed),
              sum(profiles$n_a5ss > 0), sum(profiles$n_a3ss > 0),
              sum(profiles$n_se > 0), sum(profiles$n_missing_internal > 0),
              sum(profiles$n_ir > 0), sum(profiles$n_ir_diff > 0),
              n_pir5, n_pir3)
  data.frame(event_type = evt_types,
             n_pairs_with_event = counts,
             pct_of_pairs = round(100 * counts / n_pairs, 1))
}

compute_ptc_rates_row <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  coding_ids <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]
  p_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$profiles
  cod_c2 <- p_c2[p_c2$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                   p_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
  p_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$profiles
  cod_c4 <- p_c4[p_c4$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                   p_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
  if (nrow(cod_c2) == 0 || nrow(cod_c4) == 0) return(NULL)
  ptc_c2 <- sum(cod_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE])
  ptc_c4 <- sum(cod_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE])
  n_c2 <- nrow(cod_c2); n_c4 <- nrow(cod_c4)
  ft <- tryCatch({
    mat <- matrix(c(ptc_c2, n_c2 - ptc_c2, ptc_c4, n_c4 - ptc_c4), nrow = 2)
    fisher.test(mat)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    n_coding_pairs_NMD = n_c2,
    n_coding_pairs_Ctrl = n_c4,
    NMD_comp_ptc_n = ptc_c2,
    NMD_comp_ptc_pct = round(100 * ptc_c2 / n_c2, 1),
    Ctrl_comp_ptc_n = ptc_c4,
    Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct = round(100 * ptc_c4 / n_c4, 1),
    fisher_OR = if (!is.null(ft)) round(ft$estimate, 2) else NA_real_,
    p_value = if (!is.null(ft)) ft$p.value else NA_real_
  )
}

compute_frame_category_rows <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  fc_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$frame_comp
  fc_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$frame_comp
  if (is.null(fc_c2) || is.null(fc_c4)) return(NULL)
  ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
  ps_c4 <- fc_c4$pair_summary
  cats <- c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift",
            "diff_start_same_frame", "diff_start_diff_frame",
            "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift",
            "non_coding", "no_shared_cds")
  # Denominator: coding pairs only (exclude non_coding and no_shared_cds)
  n_coding_c2 <- sum(!ps_c2$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
  n_coding_c4 <- sum(!ps_c4$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(cats, function(cat) {
    is_coding_cat <- !cat %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds")
    data.frame(
      cell_type = ct,
      frame_category = cat,
      NMD_n = sum(ps_c2$frame_category == cat),
      NMD_pct = if (is_coding_cat) round(100 * sum(ps_c2$frame_category == cat) / n_coding_c2, 1) else NA_real_,
      Ctrl_n = sum(ps_c4$frame_category == cat),
      Ctrl_pct = if (is_coding_cat) round(100 * sum(ps_c4$frame_category == cat) / n_coding_c4, 1) else NA_real_
    )
  }))
}

compute_divergence_row <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  div_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$divergence
  div_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$divergence
  if (is.null(div_c2) || nrow(div_c2) == 0 || is.null(div_c4) || nrow(div_c4) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    NMD_n = nrow(div_c2),
    NMD_median_pct_shared = round(median(div_c2$pct_shared, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Ctrl_n = nrow(div_c4),
    Ctrl_median_pct_shared = round(median(div_c4$pct_shared, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
}
```

# 0. Data Loading and Gene-Matching

## Data Provenance Overview

All analyses in this report begin from **gene-matched isoform pair sets**. The
data pipeline is:

1. **01_prepare_data_mashr.R**: Loads the isocall count matrix
   (`nmd_isocall.count_matrix.txt`, 645,273 isoforms x 38 samples), excludes
   2 outlier samples (DO donor 029T: `Sample25_DO_029T_DMSO` and
   `Sample26_DO_029T_Smg1i`, identified as PCA outlier), applies TMM
   normalization and condition-stratified 5% isoform filtering, then classifies
   isoforms as NMD-sensitive (`nmd_responsive == TRUE` in mashr DIE results) or
   non-NMD (`adj.P.Val > 0.50`). Final dataset: 36 samples across 6 cell types.
   Outputs: `expression_data.rds`, `nmd_classification.rds`,
   `sample_metadata.rds`, `gene_map.rds`.

2. **02_build_profiles_mashr.R**: Generates isoform pairs —
   **C4 (Control)**: top-two non-NMD isoforms by DMSO CPM per gene
   (`generatePairsExpression(..., method = "top_two")`);
   **C2 (NMD)**: same C4 reference paired with top NMD isoform by Smg1i CPM
   (via `identifyDominantIsoforms()` + `inner_join` on `gene_id`).
   Builds splicing choice profiles with `Isopair::buildProfiles()`.
   Outputs: `profiles_c{2,4}_*.rds`, `pairs_c{2,4}_*.rds`.

3. **03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd**: Applies **gene-matching** (restricts C2 and C4
   to genes with shared `(gene_id, reference_isoform_id)` in both sets), then
   runs Isopair analysis functions on the matched profiles. Caches results to
   `analysis_cache/`.

4. **This report (05)**: Loads profiles from step 2, re-applies gene-matching
   (step 3), loads cached analysis results, and verifies consistency. All
   downstream analyses use gene-matched profiles exclusively.

```{r load-data}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 1: Load raw data objects
# ==============================================================================

# ── 01_prepare_data_mashr.R outputs ──
# Source: isocall count matrix → TMM normalization → 5% filter → mashr NMD classification
data_dir  <- "data_mashr"
cache_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "analysis_cache")

expr_mat    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "expression_data.rds"))
sample_meta <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "sample_metadata.rds"))
gene_map    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "gene_map.rds"))
nmd_class   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "nmd_classification.rds"))

# ── Infrastructure objects (isoform-intrinsic, DE-independent) ──
# Originally from Isopair pipeline scripts 02-05, copied to data_mashr/ by
# 02_build_profiles_mashr.R for self-containment.
# structures.rds: extractIsoformStructures() — exon coordinates per isoform
# cds.rds: extractCds() — CDS boundaries per isoform
# ptc.rds: testPtcAssociation() infrastructure — PTC status per isoform
# union_exons.rds: buildUnionExons() — merged exon models per gene
# isoform_union_mapping.rds: mapIsoformsToUnion() — isoform-to-union-exon mapping
# annotated_ue.rds: annotateUnionExons() — union exons with CDS/UTR labels
# cds_exons.rds: CDS mapped to individual exons
structures   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "structures.rds"))
cds          <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "cds.rds"))
ptc          <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "ptc.rds"))
union_exons  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "union_exons.rds"))
ue_mapping   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "isoform_union_mapping.rds"))
annotated_ue <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "annotated_ue.rds"))
cds_exons    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "cds_exons.rds"))

# ── Gene symbol lookup from mashr DE files ──
de_dir_mashr <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/isocall_dge/mashr"
gene_symbol_lookup <- character(0)
for (de_f in list.files(de_dir_mashr, pattern = "^nmd_mashr_die_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)) {
  de_tmp <- read.csv(de_f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c("gene_id", "hgnc_symbol")]
  de_tmp <- de_tmp[!duplicated(de_tmp$gene_id) & !is.na(de_tmp$hgnc_symbol) &
                    de_tmp$hgnc_symbol != "", ]
  new_entries <- setdiff(de_tmp$gene_id, names(gene_symbol_lookup))
  gene_symbol_lookup[de_tmp$gene_id[de_tmp$gene_id %in% new_entries]] <-
    de_tmp$hgnc_symbol[de_tmp$gene_id %in% new_entries]
}

get_gene_sym <- function(gid) {
  sym <- gene_symbol_lookup[gid]
  if (is.na(sym) || sym == "") gid else sym
}

# Cell types (mashr: DO included, DD_ALI excluded from main)
cell_types  <- c("all_samples", "AT", "DD", "DO", "FB", "MV")
comparisons <- c("c2", "c4")
main_cts    <- c("AT", "DD", "DO", "FB", "MV")
```

```{r load-profiles}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 2: Load profiles and apply gene-matching
# ==============================================================================
#
# profiles_c{2,4}_*.rds are the output of 02_build_profiles_mashr.R. C2 pairs
# share their reference isoform with C4 (by construction in script 02), but C4
# may contain genes that have no NMD isoform (i.e., genes with >=2 non-NMD
# isoforms but no mashr-classified NMD isoform). Gene-matching restricts both
# sets to the intersection of (gene_id, reference_isoform_id), ensuring fair
# NMD vs Control comparison on identical gene sets.

profiles_list <- list()
for (ct in cell_types) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  for (comp in comparisons) {
    key <- paste(comp, ct_label, sep = "_")
    prof_file <- file.path(data_dir, sprintf("profiles_%s.rds", key))
    if (file.exists(prof_file)) profiles_list[[key]] <- readRDS(prof_file)
  }
}

# ── Gene-matching ──
# Replicates the logic from 03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd lines 743-775.
# For each cell type, restrict C2 and C4 profiles to genes where both have
# a pair with the same (gene_id, reference_isoform_id).
gene_match_summary <- list()
for (ct in cell_types) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(profiles_list) || !c4_key %in% names(profiles_list)) next

  n_c2_before <- nrow(profiles_list[[c2_key]])
  n_c4_before <- nrow(profiles_list[[c4_key]])

  c2_gene_refs <- unique(profiles_list[[c2_key]][, c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id")])
  c4_gene_refs <- unique(profiles_list[[c4_key]][, c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id")])
  shared_refs  <- dplyr::inner_join(c2_gene_refs, c4_gene_refs,
                                     by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))

  profiles_list[[c2_key]] <- dplyr::semi_join(profiles_list[[c2_key]], shared_refs,
                                               by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))
  profiles_list[[c4_key]] <- dplyr::semi_join(profiles_list[[c4_key]], shared_refs,
                                               by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))

  gene_match_summary[[ct]] <- data.frame(
    cell_type      = ct,
    c2_before      = n_c2_before,
    c4_before      = n_c4_before,
    matched_genes  = nrow(shared_refs),
    c2_after       = nrow(profiles_list[[c2_key]]),
    c4_after       = nrow(profiles_list[[c4_key]])
  )
}
gene_match_df <- do.call(rbind, gene_match_summary)
```

```{r build-set-results}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 3: Build set_results from gene-matched profiles + cached analyses
# ==============================================================================
#
# set_results[[key]] is the primary data structure for all downstream analyses.
# $profiles: gene-matched splicing choice profiles (from STAGE 2 above)
# $divergence: quantifyPairDivergence() output (cached by script 03)
# $frame_comp: compareIsoformFrames() output (cached by script 03)
# $frame_walk: analyzeFrameWalk() output (cached by script 03)
# $ptc_assoc: testPtcAssociation() output (cached by script 03)
# $evt_freq: computed here from gene-matched profiles

set_results <- list()
for (key in names(profiles_list)) {
  profiles <- profiles_list[[key]]
  set_results[[key]] <- list(
    profiles   = profiles,
    divergence = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("div_", key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    frame_comp = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("fc_",  key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    frame_walk = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("fw_",  key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    ptc_assoc  = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("ptc_", key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    evt_freq   = compute_event_freq(profiles)
  )
}

# Load divergence for all_samples (used by multiple sections)
div_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
div_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence
```

```{r verify-cache-consistency}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 4: Verify cached analysis objects match gene-matched profiles
# ==============================================================================
#
# The cached div/fc/fw/ptc objects were computed by script 03 from gene-matched
# profiles. We verify that the row counts in the cached objects match our
# gene-matched profiles_list. A mismatch would indicate the cache is stale or
# was computed from a different pair set.

verification_rows <- list()
for (key in names(set_results)) {
  sr <- set_results[[key]]
  n_profiles <- nrow(sr$profiles)

  # divergence: 1 row per pair (should exactly match profiles)
  n_div <- if (!is.null(sr$divergence)) nrow(sr$divergence) else NA
  # frame_comp$pair_summary: 1 row per pair (should exactly match)
  n_fc <- if (!is.null(sr$frame_comp)) nrow(sr$frame_comp$pair_summary) else NA
  # frame_walk$profile_summary: 1 row per pair (should exactly match)
  n_fw <- if (!is.null(sr$frame_walk)) nrow(sr$frame_walk$profile_summary) else NA
  # ptc_assoc$pair_summary: 1 row per pair where PTC analysis was possible
  #   (both isoforms coding with EJC data). Expected to be <= n_profiles.
  n_ptc <- if (!is.null(sr$ptc_assoc)) nrow(sr$ptc_assoc$pair_summary) else NA

  # Exact match expected for div, fc, fw
  div_ok <- is.na(n_div) || n_div == n_profiles
  fc_ok  <- is.na(n_fc)  || n_fc  == n_profiles
  fw_ok  <- is.na(n_fw)  || n_fw  == n_profiles
  # ptc: subset is OK (non-coding pairs excluded), but should not exceed profiles
  ptc_ok <- is.na(n_ptc) || n_ptc <= n_profiles

  verification_rows[[key]] <- data.frame(
    key = key, n_profiles = n_profiles,
    n_div = n_div, n_fc = n_fc, n_fw = n_fw, n_ptc = n_ptc,
    exact_match = div_ok & fc_ok & fw_ok,
    ptc_subset_ok = ptc_ok
  )
}
verification_df <- do.call(rbind, verification_rows)

if (!all(verification_df$exact_match)) {
  warning("CACHE MISMATCH DETECTED — div/fc/fw row counts do not match ",
          "gene-matched profiles. Affected keys: ",
          paste(verification_df$key[!verification_df$exact_match], collapse = ", "))
}
if (!all(verification_df$ptc_subset_ok)) {
  warning("PTC CACHE ANOMALY — ptc_assoc has MORE rows than profiles for: ",
          paste(verification_df$key[!verification_df$ptc_subset_ok], collapse = ", "))
}
```

# Event Type Glossary {.tabset}

Isopair detects 12 structural event types organized into 4 categories. Each tab below
shows a schematic diagram of the event alongside its definition. In all diagrams, the
**Reference** (top) is the dominant non-NMD isoform and the **Comparator** (bottom) is
the isoform being compared. Events are always described from the comparator's perspective:
a **GAIN** means the comparator has additional sequence relative to the reference, and a
**LOSS** means the comparator is missing sequence present in the reference.

**Corrections from the exploratory report (03):** A5SS and A3SS schematics were swapped;
IR_diff_5 and IR_diff_3 schematics showed the retaining exon extending beyond the reference
when the code classifies "diff" when the retaining exon falls short.

```{r glossary, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=3}
glossary_plot <- function(ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, title, subtitle,
                          ref_cds = NULL, comp_cds = NULL, events = NULL) {
  plot_ucsc_pair(ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, strand = "+",
                 ref_cds = ref_cds, comp_cds = comp_cds,
                 ref_label = "Reference", comp_label = "Comparator",
                 events = events, title = title, subtitle = subtitle)
}

# ---- Terminal Events ----

cat("## Alt_TSS\n\n")
cat("**Alternative Transcription Start Site.** The two isoforms begin at different\n")
cat("genomic positions. Detected when the 5'-most exon of one isoform does not overlap\n")
cat("the 5'-most exon of the other. Direction: GAIN if the comparator's TSS is further\n")
cat("upstream (extending the transcript); LOSS if it is further downstream (truncating it).\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(250, 400, 700), comp_e = c(350, 550, 850),
  title = "Alt_TSS: Alternative Transcription Start Site",
  subtitle = "Comparator starts at a different position (here, downstream = LOSS)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## Alt_TES\n\n")
cat("**Alternative Transcription End Site.** The two isoforms end at different\n")
cat("genomic positions. Detected when the 3'-most exon of one isoform does not overlap\n")
cat("the 3'-most exon of the other. Direction: GAIN if the comparator extends further;\n")
cat("LOSS if it ends earlier.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 900),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 550, 800),
  title = "Alt_TES: Alternative Transcription End Site",
  subtitle = "Comparator ends earlier (LOSS)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

# ---- Boundary Events ----

cat("## A5SS\n\n")
cat("**Alternative 5' Splice Site.** An internal exon has a different **donor** (exon_end\n")
cat("on + strand) boundary while sharing the same **acceptor** (exon_start) boundary.\n")
cat("The exon is extended or truncated at its downstream/3' end.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator's exon is longer; LOSS if shorter.\n\n")
# A5SS: same acceptor (exon_start=400), different donor (exon_end: 550 vs 600)
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 600, 850),
  title = "A5SS: Alternative 5' Splice Site",
  subtitle = "Same acceptor (start), different donor (end). Comparator exon extends further (GAIN)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## A3SS\n\n")
cat("**Alternative 3' Splice Site.** An internal exon has a different **acceptor** (exon_start\n")
cat("on + strand) boundary while sharing the same **donor** (exon_end) boundary.\n")
cat("The exon is extended or truncated at its upstream/5' end.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator's exon is longer; LOSS if shorter.\n\n")
# A3SS: different acceptor (exon_start: 400 vs 350), same donor (exon_end=550)
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 350, 700), comp_e = c(200, 550, 850),
  title = "A3SS: Alternative 3' Splice Site",
  subtitle = "Same donor (end), different acceptor (start). Comparator exon extends further (GAIN)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## Partial_IR_5\n\n")
cat("**Partial Intron Retention (5' end).** An intron is partially retained: one isoform's\n")
cat("exon extends into the intron from its 5' side, covering what is intronic sequence in\n")
cat("the other isoform. The 3' boundary of the retaining exon falls within the intron.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator retains; LOSS if the reference retains.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 620, 850),
  title = "Partial_IR_5: Partial Intron Retention (5' side)",
  subtitle = "Comparator exon extends into the intron from the 5' end (GAIN)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## Partial_IR_3\n\n")
cat("**Partial Intron Retention (3' end).** An intron is partially retained: one isoform's\n")
cat("exon extends into the intron from its 3' side, covering what is intronic sequence in\n")
cat("the other isoform. The 5' boundary of the retaining exon falls within the intron.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator retains; LOSS if the reference retains.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 640), comp_e = c(200, 550, 850),
  title = "Partial_IR_3: Partial Intron Retention (3' side)",
  subtitle = "Comparator exon extends into the intron from the 3' end (GAIN)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

# ---- Exon-Level Events ----

cat("## SE (Skipped Exon)\n\n")
cat("**Skipped Exon.** An exon present in one isoform is completely absent from the\n")
cat("other. The flanking exons splice directly to each other, skipping over the exon.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator includes the exon (reference skips it);\n")
cat("LOSS if the comparator skips it (reference includes it).\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 600, 800), ref_e  = c(200, 500, 700, 900),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 800),       comp_e = c(200, 500, 900),
  title = "SE: Skipped Exon",
  subtitle = "Comparator skips an internal exon present in the reference (LOSS)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## Missing_Internal\n\n")
cat("**Missing Internal Exon.** Similar to SE but arising from a multi-exon skip:\n")
cat("one isoform is missing one or more internal exons that are present in the other.\n")
cat("Often co-occurs with other Missing_Internal events from the same splice decision.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator has the exon; LOSS if the comparator lacks it.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 350, 550, 750, 950), ref_e  = c(200, 450, 650, 850, 1050),
  comp_s = c(100, 950),                 comp_e = c(200, 1050),
  title = "Missing_Internal: Missing Internal Exon(s)",
  subtitle = "Comparator skips multiple internal exons (LOSS x 3)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

# ---- Intron Retention Events ----

cat("## IR\n\n")
cat("**Full Intron Retention.** One isoform has a single exon that spans the region\n")
cat("covered by two or more exons (plus the intervening intron) in the other isoform.\n")
cat("The retaining exon boundaries match exactly. This is a full retention where the\n")
cat("entire intron is included in the retaining isoform's exon.\n")
cat("Direction: GAIN if the comparator retains the intron; LOSS if the reference retains it.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400),       comp_e = c(200, 850),
  title = "IR: Full Intron Retention",
  subtitle = "Comparator retains intron -- single exon spans two exons + intron in ref (GAIN)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## IR_diff_5\n\n")
cat("**Intron Retention with 5' Boundary Difference.** Like IR, but the retaining\n")
cat("exon's 5' boundary differs from the first overlapping exon in the other isoform.\n")
cat("The intron is retained, but the retaining exon starts after the first reference\n")
cat("overlap exon (falls short at the 5' end).\n\n")
# IR_diff_5: comp retaining exon starts AFTER first ref overlap exon start
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 430),       comp_e = c(200, 850),
  title = "IR_diff_5: Intron Retention with 5' Boundary Difference",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon starts AFTER ref overlap exon (falls short at 5' end)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## IR_diff_3\n\n")
cat("**Intron Retention with 3' Boundary Difference.** Like IR, but the retaining\n")
cat("exon's 3' boundary differs from the last overlapping exon in the other isoform.\n")
cat("The intron is retained, but the retaining exon ends before the last reference\n")
cat("overlap exon (falls short at the 3' end).\n\n")
# IR_diff_3: comp retaining exon ends BEFORE last ref overlap exon end
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400),       comp_e = c(200, 820),
  title = "IR_diff_3: Intron Retention with 3' Boundary Difference",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon ends BEFORE ref overlap exon (falls short at 3' end)")
print(p); cat("\n\n")

cat("## IR_diff_5_3\n\n")
cat("**Intron Retention with Both Boundary Differences.** Like IR, but both the 5'\n")
cat("and 3' boundaries of the retaining exon differ from the flanking exons in the\n")
cat("other isoform. The intron is retained but the retaining exon falls short at\n")
cat("both ends.\n\n")
p <- glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 430),       comp_e = c(200, 820),
  title = "IR_diff_5_3: Intron Retention with Both Boundary Differences",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon falls short at both 5' and 3' ends")
print(p); cat("\n\n")
```

In the IR section of this report, **IR_diff** refers to the aggregate of IR_diff_5,
IR_diff_3, and IR_diff_5_3 events.


# 1. Transcriptional Diversity and Isoform Optionality {#sec1-diversity}

Before asking what triggers NMD, we establish the transcriptional landscape
that NMD operates on. Genes produce diverse isoforms through combinatorial
TSS, internal splicing, and TES choices. This section characterizes
isoform diversity within the gene-matched pair set — the same genes analyzed
throughout this report. Diversity and TSS/TES analyses use all expressed
isoforms (coding and non-coding); CDS-dependent analyses are restricted to
coding isoforms.

**Data source:** All expressed isoforms for genes in the gene-matched pair
set (structures.rds, expression_data.rds). CDS analyses additionally use
cds.rds (coding isoforms only).

```{r sec1-diversity-data}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: structures.rds (extractIsoformStructures), cds.rds (extractCds),
#   expression_data.rds (TMM-normalized count matrix from 01_prepare_data_mashr.R)
# Population: All expressed isoforms for genes in gene-matched pair set.
#   Gene set defined by profiles_list (loaded in STAGE 2, gene-matched).

# Genes in the gene-matched pair set
pair_genes <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$gene_id)

# All expressed isoforms for these genes (coding + non-coding)
sec1_structures <- structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% pair_genes,
         isoform_id %in% rownames(expr_mat))

# Coding subset (for CDS-dependent analyses later)
coding_structures <- sec1_structures %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"])

coding_cds <- cds %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% coding_structures$isoform_id)

cat("Gene-matched pair genes:", length(pair_genes), "\n")
cat("All expressed isoforms (these genes):", nrow(sec1_structures), "\n")
cat("  of which coding:", nrow(coding_structures), "\n")

# ── Isoform count per gene (all isoforms) ──
iso_per_gene <- sec1_structures %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  summarise(n_isoforms = n(), .groups = "drop")

cat("\nIsoforms per gene (all expressed):\n")
print(summary(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms))
cat("Genes with ≥2 isoforms:", sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 2), "\n")
cat("Genes with ≥5 isoforms:", sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 5), "\n")
```

## Isoform Count Distribution

```{r sec1-isoform-count-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
fig_iso_count <- ggplot(iso_per_gene, aes(x = n_isoforms)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#4292c6", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 30, 5)) +
  labs(title = "Expressed Isoform Count per Gene",
       subtitle = sprintf("Gene-matched pair set | Median: %d isoforms | %s genes with ≥2",
                          median(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms),
                          format(sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 2), big.mark = ",")),
       x = "Number of expressed isoforms", y = "Number of genes")
save_fig(fig_iso_count, "fig0a_isoform_count_distribution")
```

## TSS and TES Diversity

Isoform diversity arises from three combinatorial axes: which transcription
start site (TSS) is used, which internal exons are included, and which
transcription end site (TES) is used. We quantify diversity at each axis
and ask whether TSS and TES choices are coupled or independent.

```{r sec1-tss-tes-diversity, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Multi-isoform genes only (≥2 coding isoforms)
multi_iso_genes <- iso_per_gene$gene_id[iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 2]

# ── Per-gene diversity counts (all isoforms, not just coding) ──
tss_tes <- sec1_structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes) %>%
  group_by(gene_id, strand) %>%
  summarise(
    n_isoforms = n(),
    n_unique_tss = n_distinct(ifelse(strand == "+", tx_start, tx_end)),
    n_unique_tes = n_distinct(ifelse(strand == "+", tx_end, tx_start)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("TSS diversity (multi-isoform coding genes, n =", nrow(tss_tes), "):\n")
cat("  Median distinct TSS per gene:", median(tss_tes$n_unique_tss), "\n")
cat("  Median distinct TES per gene:", median(tss_tes$n_unique_tes), "\n")

# ── Within-gene TSS-TES independence ──
# The key question: for a given gene, does knowing which TSS is used
# predict which TES is used? We compute per-gene Spearman rho between
# TSS and TES positions across isoforms.
within_gene_cor <- sec1_structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes) %>%
  mutate(
    tss = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_start, tx_end),
    tes = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_end, tx_start)
  ) %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3, n_distinct(tss) >= 2, n_distinct(tes) >= 2) %>%
  summarise(
    n_iso = n(),
    rho_tss_tes = cor(tss, tes, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

within_gene_rho <- median(within_gene_cor$rho_tss_tes, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("\nWithin-gene TSS-TES coupling (n =", nrow(within_gene_cor), "genes with ≥3 iso):\n")
cat("  Median Spearman rho:", round(within_gene_rho, 3), "\n")
cat("  Mean Spearman rho:", round(mean(within_gene_cor$rho_tss_tes, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  IQR:", round(quantile(within_gene_cor$rho_tss_tes, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    "to", round(quantile(within_gene_cor$rho_tss_tes, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")

# ── Combination usage ──
# If TSS and TES were fully independent and all combinations viable,
# genes would use ~100% of TSS×TES pairs. Selective usage indicates
# the exon path constrains which TSS-TES pairings are realized.
tss_tes_combos <- sec1_structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes) %>%
  mutate(
    tss = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_start, tx_end),
    tes = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_end, tx_start)
  ) %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tss = n_distinct(tss),
    n_tes = n_distinct(tes),
    n_combos = n_distinct(paste(tss, tes)),
    max_possible = n_distinct(tss) * n_distinct(tes),
    pct_used = round(100 * n_distinct(paste(tss, tes)) /
                       (n_distinct(tss) * n_distinct(tes)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(max_possible > 1)

cat("\nTSS×TES combination usage (n =", nrow(tss_tes_combos), "genes):\n")
cat("  Median % of possible combinations used:", round(median(tss_tes_combos$pct_used), 1), "%\n")
cat("  Mean:", round(mean(tss_tes_combos$pct_used), 1), "%\n")

# ── Figures ──

# Panel A: TSS and TES count distributions
tss_tes_long <- tss_tes %>%
  select(gene_id, TSS = n_unique_tss, TES = n_unique_tes) %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene_id, names_to = "feature", values_to = "count")

p_diversity <- ggplot(tss_tes_long, aes(x = count, fill = feature)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, position = "dodge", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 20), breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(TSS = "#ef8a62", TES = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "A. TSS and TES Diversity per Gene",
       subtitle = sprintf("Multi-isoform coding genes (n = %s)",
                          format(nrow(tss_tes), big.mark = ",")),
       x = "Number of distinct positions", y = "Number of genes", fill = "")

# Panel B: Within-gene TSS-TES correlation distribution
p_within <- ggplot(within_gene_cor, aes(x = rho_tss_tes)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "#756bb1", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = within_gene_rho, color = "#e6550d", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = within_gene_rho + 0.05, y = Inf, vjust = 2,
           label = sprintf("median = %.3f", within_gene_rho),
           color = "#e6550d", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  labs(title = "B. Within-Gene TSS-TES Coupling",
       subtitle = sprintf("Per-gene Spearman rho (n = %s genes with ≥3 isoforms)",
                          format(nrow(within_gene_cor), big.mark = ",")),
       x = "Spearman rho (TSS position vs TES position)", y = "Number of genes")

# Panel C: Combination usage
p_combos <- ggplot(tss_tes_combos, aes(x = pct_used)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "#31a354", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(tss_tes_combos$pct_used), color = "#e6550d", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = median(tss_tes_combos$pct_used) + 2, y = Inf, vjust = 2,
           label = sprintf("median = %.0f%%", median(tss_tes_combos$pct_used)),
           color = "#e6550d", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  labs(title = "C. TSS × TES Combination Usage",
       subtitle = "% of possible TSS-TES pairs actually observed",
       x = "Combinations used (%)", y = "Number of genes")

fig_tss_tes <- p_diversity / (p_within | p_combos)
save_fig(fig_tss_tes, "fig0b_tss_tes_diversity", width = 10, height = 8)
```

Within any given gene, the TSS and TES positions are largely independent:
the median within-gene Spearman rho is `r round(within_gene_rho, 3)`,
centered tightly around zero. Knowing which promoter a transcript initiates
from does not predict where it will terminate.

Yet genes use only `r round(median(tss_tes_combos$pct_used))`% of the
TSS×TES combinations that would be possible if every start could pair with
every end. This apparent contradiction resolves when we consider the exon
path: internal splicing decisions constrain which TSS-TES pairings produce
viable transcripts. TSS and TES are chosen independently of *each other*,
but the internal exon structure acts as a filter — not all combinations
produce stable, processable transcripts.

## TSS–CDS and TES–CDS Coupling

```{r sec1-tss-cds-coupling}
# TSS determines CDS start; TES determines CDS stop
coupling <- coding_structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes) %>%
  inner_join(coding_cds %>% select(isoform_id, cds_start, cds_stop),
             by = "isoform_id") %>%
  mutate(
    tss = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_start, tx_end),
    tes = ifelse(strand == "+", tx_end, tx_start),
    cds_5prime = ifelse(strand == "+", cds_start, cds_stop),
    cds_3prime = ifelse(strand == "+", cds_stop, cds_start)
  )

# Per-gene correlations (genes with ≥3 isoforms for meaningful correlation)
gene_cors <- coupling %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  summarise(
    n_iso = n(),
    rho_tss_cds5 = cor(tss, cds_5prime, method = "spearman"),
    rho_tes_cds3 = cor(tes, cds_3prime, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("TSS → CDS start coupling (per-gene Spearman rho):\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(gene_cors$rho_tss_cds5, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  Mean:", round(mean(gene_cors$rho_tss_cds5, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")

cat("\nTES → CDS stop coupling:\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(gene_cors$rho_tes_cds3, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  Mean:", round(mean(gene_cors$rho_tes_cds3, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
```

The TSS strongly determines the CDS start position, and the TES strongly
determines the CDS stop position. The two ends of the protein are set by
the two ends of the transcript — through the exon path, not directly.

## CDS Start Diversity and Reading Frame Multiplicity

```{r sec1-cds-start-diversity}
# How many distinct CDS start positions per gene? (coding isoforms only)
cds_diversity <- coding_structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes) %>%
  inner_join(coding_cds %>% select(isoform_id, cds_start, cds_stop),
             by = "isoform_id") %>%
  mutate(cds_5prime = ifelse(strand == "+", cds_start, cds_stop)) %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  summarise(
    n_isoforms = n(),
    n_cds_starts = n_distinct(cds_5prime),
    cds_starts = list(unique(cds_5prime)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("CDS start diversity (multi-coding-isoform genes, n =", nrow(cds_diversity), "):\n")
cat("  Genes with ≥2 distinct CDS starts:",
    sum(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts >= 2),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts >= 2)))
cat("  Genes with ≥3 distinct CDS starts:",
    sum(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts >= 3),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts >= 3)))
cat("  Median distinct CDS starts:", median(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts), "\n")

# Of genes with multiple CDS starts, how many use different reading frames?
# Two CDS starts are in different frames if their positions differ by a non-multiple of 3.
cds_diversity$has_diff_frame <- sapply(cds_diversity$cds_starts, function(s) {
  if (length(s) < 2) return(FALSE)
  diffs <- outer(s, s, "-")
  diffs <- diffs[upper.tri(diffs)]
  any(diffs %% 3 != 0)
})

multi_start <- cds_diversity %>% filter(n_cds_starts >= 2)
cat("\nReading frame diversity (genes with ≥2 CDS starts, n =", nrow(multi_start), "):\n")
cat("  Genes with starts in DIFFERENT frames:",
    sum(multi_start$has_diff_frame),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(multi_start$has_diff_frame)))
cat("  Genes with all starts in SAME frame:",
    sum(!multi_start$has_diff_frame),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(!multi_start$has_diff_frame)))
```

`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(cds_diversity$n_cds_starts >= 2))` of genes
with multiple coding isoforms use at least two distinct CDS start positions.
Among these, `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(multi_start$has_diff_frame))`
use CDS starts in different reading frames — the start positions differ by a
non-multiple of 3, meaning the downstream protein sequences are in different
frames. These genes encode genuinely distinct reading frames through their
isoform repertoire, not merely N-terminal extensions of the same protein.

## Expression Concentration

```{r sec1-expression-concentration}
# How much of a gene's output comes from its dominant isoform?
# Use DMSO samples for baseline expression
dmso_samples <- sample_meta$sample_id[sample_meta$treatment == "DMSO"]
dmso_mat <- expr_mat[, colnames(expr_mat) %in% dmso_samples]

# CPM per isoform
lib_sizes <- colSums(dmso_mat)
cpm_mat <- sweep(dmso_mat, 2, lib_sizes, "/") * 1e6

# Per-gene dominant fraction
gene_ids <- coding_structures$gene_id[match(rownames(cpm_mat), coding_structures$isoform_id)]
valid <- !is.na(gene_ids) & rownames(cpm_mat) %in% coding_structures$isoform_id

mean_cpm <- rowMeans(cpm_mat[valid, ])
iso_df <- data.frame(
  isoform_id = rownames(cpm_mat)[valid],
  gene_id = gene_ids[valid],
  mean_cpm = mean_cpm,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dominant_fraction <- iso_df %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2, sum(mean_cpm) > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    n_iso = n(),
    total_cpm = sum(mean_cpm),
    max_cpm = max(mean_cpm),
    dominant_pct = 100 * max_cpm / total_cpm,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Expression concentration (DMSO, multi-isoform coding genes):\n")
cat("  Median dominant isoform share:", round(median(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct), 1), "%\n")
cat("  Genes where dominant >50%:", sum(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 50),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 50)))
cat("  Genes where dominant >80%:", sum(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 80),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 80)))
```

Transcriptional diversity is the norm. Genes maintain multiple exon paths,
each producing a different reading frame context. Most genes concentrate
expression on a dominant isoform, but devote substantial transcriptional
output to alternatives — including paths that produce NMD substrates.

# 1b. Baseline Splicing and NMD-Enriched Events {#goal1b-baseline}

Characterize baseline alternative splicing (Control C4 pairs) and identify which
splicing event types are enriched in NMD vs Control.

**Methods:** Structural profiles quantify splicing event types for each pair. Sequence
divergence (`quantifyPairDivergence()`) measures exonic sequence shared between isoforms.
NMD vs Control enrichment is tested by Fisher's exact test per event type.

## Figure 1: Sequence Shared — NMD vs Control

```{r goal1-fig1-pct-shared, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles → cached divergence
# div_c2 = set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
#   Source: quantifyPairDivergence(gene-matched profiles, structures, cds),
#   cached by script 03
#   $pct_shared: percentage of exonic sequence shared between ref and comp
# div_c4: same for Control
# Result: density comparison of sequence similarity between NMD and Control pairs

pct_shared_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(comparison = "NMD",     pct_shared = div_c2$pct_shared),
  data.frame(comparison = "Control", pct_shared = div_c4$pct_shared))
pct_shared_data <- pct_shared_data[!is.na(pct_shared_data$pct_shared), ]

fig1_shared <- ggplot(pct_shared_data, aes(x = pct_shared, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Exonic Sequence Shared (%): NMD vs Control",
       subtitle = "NMD pairs shifted right = more similar (targeted splicing changes)",
       x = "Sequence Shared (%)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig1_shared, "fig1_pct_shared_density")

# Summary stats
shared_summary <- pct_shared_data |>
  group_by(comparison) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median = round(median(pct_shared), 1),
            mean = round(mean(pct_shared), 1), .groups = "drop")
render_dt(shared_summary, caption = "Table 1a: Sequence Shared Summary")
```

Columns: **comparison** = NMD or Control; **n** = number of pairs; **median/mean** =
median and mean percentage of exonic sequence shared between reference and
comparator (from `Isopair::quantifyPairDivergence()`).

## Table 1b: Splicing Event Enrichment — NMD vs Control

For each event type, the denominator is all gene-matched pairs (not restricted
to coding) — a pair is counted if it has ≥1 event of that type. Fisher's exact
test compares the proportion of pairs with each event type between NMD (C2) and
Control (C4), both on the same gene-matched set.

```{r goal1-table1b-event-enrichment}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (set_results[[key]]$profiles)
# compute_event_freq(profiles) counts pairs with each event type using:
#   - Boolean columns (tss_changed, tes_changed, n_a5ss > 0, etc.) from profiles
#   - Partial_IR_5/3 from detailed_events list-column
#   These are computed by buildProfiles → compareSplicingChoices
# Fisher's exact test: event prevalence in NMD vs Control on gene-matched sets

ef_c2 <- compute_event_freq(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
ef_c4 <- compute_event_freq(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_c2 <- nrow(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_c4 <- nrow(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)

enrichment <- merge(ef_c2, ef_c4, by = "event_type", suffixes = c("_NMD", "_Ctrl"))

# Fisher's exact test per event type
enrichment$fisher_OR <- NA_real_
enrichment$fisher_p <- NA_real_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(enrichment))) {
  a <- enrichment$n_pairs_with_event_NMD[i]
  b <- n_c2 - a
  c <- enrichment$n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl[i]
  d <- n_c4 - c
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, c, d), nrow = 2)), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    enrichment$fisher_OR[i] <- round(ft$estimate, 2)
    enrichment$fisher_p[i] <- ft$p.value
  }
}

enrichment$direction <- ifelse(enrichment$fisher_p > 0.05, "Non-significant",
  ifelse(enrichment$fisher_OR > 1, "Enriched in NMD", "Enriched in Control"))
enrichment <- enrichment[order(enrichment$fisher_p), ]

enrich_display <- enrichment[, c("event_type", "n_pairs_with_event_NMD", "pct_of_pairs_NMD",
                                 "n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl", "pct_of_pairs_Ctrl",
                                 "fisher_OR", "fisher_p", "direction")]
enrich_display$fisher_p <- signif(enrich_display$fisher_p, 3)
render_dt(enrich_display,
          caption = "Table 1b: Splicing Event Type Enrichment — NMD vs Control")
write.csv(enrichment, file.path(table_dir, "table1b_event_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **event_type** = splicing event type (see Event Type Glossary);
**n_pairs_with_event_NMD** = number of gene-matched NMD (C2) pairs with ≥1
event of this type; **pct_of_pairs_NMD** = percentage of all
`r fmt(n_c2)` NMD pairs; **n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl/pct_of_pairs_Ctrl** =
same for Control (C4, `r fmt(n_c4)` pairs); **fisher_OR** = Fisher's exact
test odds ratio (>1 = NMD-enriched); **fisher_p** = p-value; **direction** =
Enriched in NMD, Enriched in Control, or Non-significant (p > 0.05).

### Figure 1b: Splicing Event Prevalence — NMD vs Control

```{r goal1-fig1b-event-barplot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# enrichment: from goal1-table1b-event-enrichment chunk
# Paired barplot of event prevalence (% of pairs) by comparison type

bar_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(event_type = enrichment$event_type,
             comparison = "NMD",
             pct = enrichment$pct_of_pairs_NMD),
  data.frame(event_type = enrichment$event_type,
             comparison = "Control",
             pct = enrichment$pct_of_pairs_Ctrl))

# Order events by NMD prevalence (descending)
evt_order <- enrichment$event_type[order(-enrichment$pct_of_pairs_NMD)]
bar_df$event_type <- factor(bar_df$event_type, levels = evt_order)

# Significance stars
sig_df <- data.frame(
  event_type = factor(enrichment$event_type, levels = evt_order),
  y = pmax(enrichment$pct_of_pairs_NMD, enrichment$pct_of_pairs_Ctrl) + 2,
  label = ifelse(enrichment$fisher_p < 0.001, "***",
           ifelse(enrichment$fisher_p < 0.01, "**",
             ifelse(enrichment$fisher_p < 0.05, "*", "ns"))))

fig1b <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = event_type, y = pct, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = sig_df, aes(x = event_type, y = y, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Splicing Event Prevalence: NMD vs Control",
       subtitle = sprintf("NMD: %s pairs, Control: %s pairs. Significance: Fisher's exact test (* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001).",
                           fmt(n_c2), fmt(n_c4)),
       x = "", y = "% of Pairs with Event", fill = "Comparison") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")

save_fig(fig1b, "fig1b_event_prevalence_barplot", width = 10, height = 6)
```

## Table 1c: Gain/Loss Direction by Event Type

For each event type, the comparator can GAIN sequence (comparator has additional
sequence relative to reference) or LOSE sequence (comparator is missing sequence
present in reference). The table below shows event counts and the percentage of
events in each direction, separately for NMD and Control pairs.

```{r goal1-table1c-gain-loss}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (set_results[[key]]$profiles)
# $detailed_events: list-column, one data.frame per pair from buildProfiles
#   Each event row has event_type and direction (GAIN or LOSS)
#   Direction is from comparator's perspective (see Event Type Glossary)
# For each comparison (NMD, Control): count events by type × direction,
#   compute % GAIN and % LOSS within each event type

get_gain_loss_pct <- function(profiles, label) {
  all_events <- do.call(rbind, profiles$detailed_events)
  if (is.null(all_events) || nrow(all_events) == 0) return(NULL)
  gl <- all_events |>
    group_by(event_type, direction) |>
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  totals <- gl |> group_by(event_type) |> summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  gl <- merge(gl, totals, by = "event_type")
  gl$pct <- round(100 * gl$n / gl$total, 1)
  gl$comparison <- label
  gl
}

gl_c2 <- get_gain_loss_pct(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles, "NMD")
gl_c4 <- get_gain_loss_pct(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles, "Control")
gl_all <- rbind(gl_c2, gl_c4)

gl_wide <- gl_all |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = event_type,
    names_from = c(comparison, direction),
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(event_type)

col_order <- c("event_type",
  "n_NMD_GAIN", "n_NMD_LOSS", "pct_NMD_GAIN",
  "n_Control_GAIN", "n_Control_LOSS", "pct_Control_GAIN")
existing_cols <- intersect(col_order, names(gl_wide))
gl_display <- gl_wide[, existing_cols, drop = FALSE]

gl_display$fisher_p <- NA_real_
gl_display$direction_diff <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gl_display))) {
  ng <- gl_display$n_NMD_GAIN[i]
  nl <- gl_display$n_NMD_LOSS[i]
  cg <- gl_display$n_Control_GAIN[i]
  cl <- gl_display$n_Control_LOSS[i]
  if (ng + nl > 0 && cg + cl > 0) {
    ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(ng, nl, cg, cl), nrow = 2)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(ft)) {
      gl_display$fisher_p[i] <- signif(ft$p.value, 3)
      pct_nmd <- 100 * ng / (ng + nl)
      pct_ctrl <- 100 * cg / (cg + cl)
      gl_display$direction_diff[i] <- if (ft$p.value > 0.05) "Non-significant"
        else if (pct_nmd > pct_ctrl) "More GAIN in NMD"
        else "More LOSS in NMD"
    }
  }
}

render_dt(gl_display, caption = "Table 1c: Gain/Loss Events by Type — NMD vs Control")
write.csv(gl_display, file.path(table_dir, "table1c_gain_loss_events.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **event_type** = splicing event type; **n_NMD_GAIN/n_NMD_LOSS** =
count of NMD events with GAIN/LOSS direction (from comparator's perspective);
**pct_NMD_GAIN** = percentage of NMD events of that type with GAIN direction;
**n_Control_GAIN/n_Control_LOSS/pct_Control_GAIN** = same for Control;
**fisher_p** = Fisher's exact test p-value comparing GAIN/LOSS ratio between
NMD and Control; **direction_diff** = "More GAIN in NMD", "More LOSS in NMD",
or "Non-significant" (p > 0.05).

### Figure 1c: GAIN Direction by Event Type — NMD vs Control

```{r goal1-fig1c-gain-loss-barplot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

bar1c <- rbind(

             comparison = "NMD",

  data.frame(event_type = gl_display$event_type,
             comparison = "Control",
             pct_gain = gl_display$pct_Control_GAIN))

# Order events by NMD % GAIN (descending)
evt_order_1c <- gl_display$event_type[order(-gl_display$pct_NMD_GAIN)]
bar1c$event_type <- factor(bar1c$event_type, levels = evt_order_1c)

# Significance stars

fig1c <- ggplot(bar1c, aes(x = event_type, y = pct_gain, fill = comparison)) +

  labs(title = "GAIN Direction by Event Type: NMD vs Control",

       x = "", y = "% Events with GAIN Direction", fill = "Comparison") +
```

# 2a. Predicting NMD from Isoform Structure — The Unified Model {#sec2a-unified}

Can we predict which isoforms trigger NMD from structural features alone?
We build a model progressively, adding feature categories and measuring
improvement. This overview presents the unified model; subsequent sections
drill into each feature category.

**Data source:** All mashr-classified NMD and non-NMD coding isoforms with
complete structural features (broader than the paired framework). The model
asks "can structural features predict NMD status?" — an isoform-level
question, not a pair-level question.

**Statistical approach:** Elastic net logistic regression (alpha = 0.5) with
10-fold cross-validation on the training set. Holdout chromosomes 1, 3, 5, 7
(~26% of data) are never used for feature selection or model tuning.

```{r sec2a-load-model}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: 05l_unified_model.R → unified_model.rds
# Population: ALL mashr-classified NMD/non-NMD coding isoforms with complete
#   structural features (PTC from ptc.rds, 5'UTR from utr5_features_all.rds)
# Train/test: holdout chr 1, 3, 5, 7 (~26%)

unified <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "unified_model.rds"))

cat("Population:", format(unified$metadata$population, big.mark = ","),
    "isoforms with complete features\n")
cat("NMD:", sum(unified$df$is_nmd),
    "| Non-NMD:", sum(!unified$df$is_nmd), "\n")
cat("Holdout chromosomes:", paste(unified$metadata$holdout_chrs, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Feature name mapping for display
feat_labels <- unified$feature_labels
```

## Progressive ROC Curves

```{r sec2a-progressive-roc, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: unified$elastic_net (elastic net models fit on training data)
# ROC curves from stored roc_test objects (holdout predictions)

en_models <- list(
  list(roc = unified$elastic_net$step1$roc_test,
       name = "Step 1: Stop codon position", color = "#fc8d59"),
  list(roc = unified$elastic_net$step2$roc_test,
       name = "Step 2: + Start codon context", color = "#91bfdb"),
  list(roc = unified$elastic_net$step3$roc_test,
       name = "Step 3: + ORF features (unified)", color = "#1a1a1a")
)

roc_curves <- lapply(en_models, function(spec) {
  auc_val <- as.numeric(auc(spec$roc))
  data.frame(
    fpr = 1 - spec$roc$specificities,
    tpr = spec$roc$sensitivities,
    model = sprintf("%s (AUC = %.3f)", spec$name, auc_val),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
roc_all <- do.call(rbind, roc_curves)
roc_all$model <- factor(roc_all$model, levels = unique(roc_all$model))

model_colors <- setNames(
  sapply(en_models, `[[`, "color"),
  levels(roc_all$model)
)

fig_roc <- ggplot(roc_all, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, color = model)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = model_colors) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Holdout ROC — Progressive Model Building",
       subtitle = sprintf("Holdout: chr 1, 3, 5, 7 (N = %s)",
                          format(unified$elastic_net$step3$n_test, big.mark = ",")),
       x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate",
       color = "") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.62, 0.18),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "grey80"),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))
save_fig(fig_roc, "fig_progressive_roc", width = 7, height = 7)
```

Each curve represents a progressive elastic net model evaluated on the
holdout chromosomes. Stop codon position alone (the stepped orange curve)
reflects the 4-level categorical predictor — it achieves coarse but
meaningful discrimination (AUC =
`r round(unified$elastic_net$step1$auc_test, 3)`). Adding start codon
features produces a smooth curve with substantially improved sensitivity
across all specificity levels. The final unified model (black) adds ORF
features for further gains, particularly in the high-specificity region.

## Feature Importance

```{r sec2a-coefficients}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: unified$elastic_net$step3$cv_fit (elastic net, unified model)
# Non-zero coefficients at lambda.min, sorted by absolute magnitude

en_fit <- unified$elastic_net$step3$cv_fit
coefs <- as.matrix(coef(en_fit, s = "lambda.min"))
nonzero <- coefs[coefs[, 1] != 0 & rownames(coefs) != "(Intercept)", , drop = FALSE]

coef_table <- data.frame(
  r_name = rownames(nonzero),
  Coefficient = nonzero[, 1],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    Feature = ifelse(r_name %in% names(feat_labels),
                     feat_labels[r_name], r_name),
    `Abs. Coefficient` = abs(Coefficient)
  ) %>%
  arrange(-`Abs. Coefficient`) %>%
  transmute(Feature, Coefficient = round(Coefficient, 4))

render_dt(coef_table, caption = "Table: Elastic Net Feature Importance (Unified Model)")
```

Column definitions: **Feature** = model variable (display name);
**Coefficient** = elastic net coefficient at lambda.min (standardized
features). Positive coefficients increase predicted NMD probability;
negative coefficients decrease it. Features with zero coefficients are
excluded by the elastic net penalty.

## Complementarity: Stop Codon vs Start Codon Features

```{r sec2a-complementarity}
# Stop-codon-only vs 5'UTR-only vs combined
comp_df <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Stop codon only", "5'UTR only", "Combined"),
  `Train AUC` = round(c(
    unified$elastic_net$step1$auc_train,
    unified$elastic_net$utr5_only$auc_train,
    unified$elastic_net$step3$auc_train
  ), 3),
  `Test AUC` = round(c(
    unified$elastic_net$step1$auc_test,
    unified$elastic_net$utr5_only$auc_test,
    unified$elastic_net$step3$auc_test
  ), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
render_dt(comp_df, caption = "Complementarity: Feature Sets Alone vs Combined")
```

Column definitions: **Model** = feature set used; **Train AUC** = AUC on
training chromosomes; **Test AUC** = AUC on holdout chromosomes (1, 3, 5, 7).

Stop codon and start codon features are complementary, not redundant. Each
achieves comparable AUC alone (~0.70–0.72), but combined they reach
`r round(unified$elastic_net$step3$auc_test, 3)`. This means PTC and uORF
mechanisms operate through different structural pathways to trigger NMD.

# 2b. Stop Codons: Where Translation Terminates {#sec2b-stop-codons}

The strongest single feature category is the downstream EJC count. Here we
examine stop codon position in detail using gene-matched C2 (NMD) vs C4
(Control) isoform pairs.

**Methods:** A PTC is defined as a stop codon >50 nt upstream of the last exon-junction
complex (EJC). Fisher's exact test compares PTC rates between NMD (C2) and Control (C4)
comparator isoforms, restricted to pairs where both reference and comparator are coding.
PTC position metrics (distance to EJC, % CDS, number of downstream EJCs) characterize NMD
response strength using mashr meta-analysis posterior means averaged across 5 conditions
(DD, AT, DO_ALI, FB, MV).

## PTC Rates

```{r goal1-ptc-rates-subsetting}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (profiles_list → set_results$profiles)
#   Pipeline: 01 (mashr NMD classification) → 02 (pair generation + buildProfiles)
#   → gene-matching (this report, STAGE 2) → set_results (STAGE 3)
#
# Subsetting for PTC rate calculation:
#   1. Start with gene-matched C2 (NMD) and C4 (Control) profiles
#   2. Restrict to "coding pairs": both reference AND comparator isoform must have
#      coding_status == "coding" in cds.rds (from Isopair extractCds() on SQANTI CDS)
#   3. Numerator: comparator isoforms with has_ptc == TRUE in ptc.rds
#      PTC definition: stop codon >50 nt upstream of the last exon-junction complex (EJC)
#   4. Denominator: total coding pairs (from step 2)
#   5. Fisher's exact test: 2×2 table of (PTC+/PTC−) × (NMD/Control)

# Show the subsetting explicitly
coding_ids <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]
n_gm_c2 <- nrow(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_gm_c4 <- nrow(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)

p_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles
cod_c2 <- p_c2[p_c2$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                p_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
p_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles
cod_c4 <- p_c4[p_c4$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                p_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
```

Starting from `r fmt(n_gm_c2)` gene-matched NMD (C2) pairs and
`r fmt(n_gm_c4)` gene-matched Control (C4) pairs, we restrict to **coding
pairs** where both the reference and comparator isoform are classified as
protein-coding by SQANTI (`coding_status == "coding"` in `cds.rds`). This
yields `r fmt(nrow(cod_c2))` coding NMD pairs and `r fmt(nrow(cod_c4))` coding
Control pairs. The PTC rate is the fraction of these coding comparator isoforms
whose stop codon falls >50 nt upstream of the last exon-junction complex (EJC),
as computed by `Isopair::testPtcAssociation()`.

```{r goal1-ptc-rates}
ptc_rates <- compute_ptc_rates_row("all_samples")
kable(ptc_rates, caption = "Table 2: PTC Rates — all_samples",
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 2))
write.csv(ptc_rates, file.path(table_dir, "table2_ptc_rates_allsamples.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **cell_type** = sample set; **n_coding_pairs_NMD/Ctrl** = number of
coding pairs (both ref and comp coding) in NMD (C2) / Control (C4);
**NMD_comp_ptc_n/pct** = count and percentage of NMD comparators with PTC;
**Ctrl_comp_ptc_n/pct** = same for Control; **fisher_OR** = odds ratio from
Fisher's exact test; **p_value** = Fisher p-value.

## Figure 2: Stop Codon Distance to Last EJC

```{r goal1-fig1-stop-dist-pop}
# ── Population derivation ──
# Start from gene-matched comparators, filter to those with non-NA ptc_distance.
# This is broader than Table 2 (not restricted to coding pairs).
fig2_pop <- list()
for (comp in c("c2", "c4")) {
  key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
  comp_ids <- set_results[[key]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id
  n_total <- length(comp_ids)
  ptc_sub <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% comp_ids & !is.na(ptc$ptc_distance), ]
  fig2_pop[[comp]] <- list(n_total = n_total, n_with_dist = nrow(ptc_sub))
}
```

Starting from `r fmt(fig2_pop$c2$n_total)` gene-matched NMD comparators,
`r fmt(fig2_pop$c2$n_with_dist)` have a non-NA `ptc_distance` in `ptc.rds`
(i.e., have an annotated CDS with a stop codon and ≥1 exon-junction complex).
For Control: `r fmt(fig2_pop$c4$n_with_dist)` of `r fmt(fig2_pop$c4$n_total)`.
This is a broader set than Table 2, which additionally requires **both**
reference and comparator to be coding (pair-level filter). Here only the
comparator needs `ptc_distance` (isoform-level filter).

```{r goal1-fig1-stop-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
stop_dist_all <- {
  rows <- list()
  for (comp in c("c2", "c4")) {
    key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
    comp_ids <- set_results[[key]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id
    ptc_sub <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% comp_ids & !is.na(ptc$ptc_distance), ]
    if (nrow(ptc_sub) == 0) next
    rows[[comp]] <- data.frame(
      comparison = comp_label(comp),
      ptc_distance = ptc_sub$ptc_distance,
      has_ptc = ptc_sub$has_ptc)
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

fig1 <- ggplot(stop_dist_all, aes(x = ptc_distance, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 50, y = Inf, label = "PTC threshold (50 nt)",
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(
    quantile(stop_dist_all$ptc_distance, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(stop_dist_all$ptc_distance, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Stop Codon Distance to Last EJC: NMD vs Control Comparators",
       subtitle = "All comparator isoforms with annotated stop codon + EJC. Dashed red = 50 nt PTC threshold.",
       x = "Distance from stop codon to last EJC (nt)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig1, "fig2_stop_codon_distance")
```

## Figure 3: NMD Response vs Stop Codon Distance

```{r goal1-fig2-logfc-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 all_samples profiles
# Step 1: Extract comparator_isoform_id from gene-matched C2 profiles
# Step 2: Look up ptc features (ptc_distance, has_ptc, orf_length, n_downstream_ejcs)
#   from ptc.rds for those comparators
# Step 3: Merge with meta_logfc — mashr PosteriorMean averaged across 5 conditions
#   (DD, AT, DO_ALI, FB, MV). Source: mashr_isoform_model_2026.3.10.rds
# Result: scatter of NMD response magnitude vs stop codon position

comp_ids_as <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id
ptc_sub <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% comp_ids_as & !is.na(ptc$ptc_distance),
                c("isoform_id", "ptc_distance", "has_ptc", "orf_length", "n_downstream_ejcs")]
n_with_logfc <- sum(comp_ids_as %in% meta_logfc$txid)
nmd_logfc_dist <- merge(meta_logfc[meta_logfc$txid %in% comp_ids_as, ],
                         ptc_sub, by.x = "txid", by.y = "isoform_id")
```

Of `r fmt(length(comp_ids_as))` gene-matched NMD comparators,
`r fmt(nrow(ptc_sub))` have non-NA `ptc_distance` and
`r fmt(n_with_logfc)` have a mashr posterior mean logFC. After merging
(requiring both), `r fmt(nrow(nmd_logfc_dist))` comparators remain.
`r if (length(comp_ids_as) - n_with_logfc > 0) paste0("The ", fmt(length(comp_ids_as) - n_with_logfc), " comparators absent from the mashr model are novel isoforms not tested for differential expression.") else "All comparators have mashr logFC values."`

```{r goal1-fig2-logfc-dist-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
fig2 <- ggplot(nmd_logfc_dist, aes(x = ptc_distance, y = mean_logFC)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(
    quantile(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) +
  labs(title = sprintf("NMD Response vs Stop Codon Distance (n = %d)", nrow(nmd_logfc_dist)),
       subtitle = "mashr meta-analysis mean logFC (5 conditions). Blue = loess.",
       x = "Distance from stop codon to last EJC (nt)",
       y = "Mean logFC (mashr)")
save_fig(fig2, "fig3_nmd_response_vs_distance")

# Correlation summary
cor_test <- cor.test(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, nmd_logfc_dist$mean_logFC,
                      method = "spearman")
kable(data.frame(n = nrow(nmd_logfc_dist),
                 spearman_rho = round(cor_test$estimate, 3),
                 p_value = cor_test$p.value),
      caption = "Spearman correlation: Stop-to-EJC distance vs mean logFC")
```

## How PTCs Arise: Splicing Mechanisms {#sec2b-ptc-mechanisms}

**Goal 3:** Identify the splicing mechanisms that produce PTCs in NMD-responsive isoforms.

**Methods:** Frame comparison (`compareIsoformFrames()`) classifies each pair by start codon
and reading frame relationship. Frame walk (`analyzeFrameWalk()`) identifies which splicing
events cause frameshifts. The Sankey diagram traces flows from splice event type through frame
category to PTC outcome for NMD comparators.

## Figure 5: Frame Category Distribution

```{r goal2-fig4-pop}
# Count excluded categories for prose
fc_c2_ps <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$frame_comp$pair_summary
fc_c4_ps <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$frame_comp$pair_summary
n_noncoding_c2 <- sum(fc_c2_ps$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
n_noncoding_c4 <- sum(fc_c4_ps$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
```

`compareIsoformFrames()` assigns each pair a frame category based on start codon
and reading frame relationship. Of `r fmt(nrow(fc_c2_ps))` NMD pairs,
`r fmt(n_noncoding_c2)` are classified as `non_coding` or `no_shared_cds` and
excluded from the figure (Control: `r fmt(n_noncoding_c4)` of
`r fmt(nrow(fc_c4_ps))` excluded). The denominator (y-axis) is the number of
**coding pairs** (`r fmt(nrow(fc_c2_ps) - n_noncoding_c2)` NMD,
`r fmt(nrow(fc_c4_ps) - n_noncoding_c4)` Control), so the 5 categories sum
to 100%.

```{r goal2-fig4-frame-category, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles → cached frame comparison
# set_results[[key]]$frame_comp: compareIsoformFrames() output, cached by script 03
#   Input to compareIsoformFrames(): gene-matched profiles + cds_exons.rds + cds.rds
#   $pair_summary contains frame_category per pair (same_start_in_frame, same_start_frameshift, etc.)
# ptc.rds$has_ptc: PTC status per isoform (isoform-intrinsic, independent of pairing)
# Denominator (total_pairs): nrow(gene-matched profiles) — ensures consistent
#   percentages between profiles and frame_comp (verified in STAGE 4)

coding_cats <- c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift",
                 "diff_start_same_frame", "diff_start_diff_frame",
                 "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")
cat_labels <- c(
  same_start_in_frame = "Same Start\nSame Frame",
  same_start_frameshift = "Same Start\nFrameshift",
  diff_start_same_frame = "Diff Start\nSame Frame",
  diff_start_diff_frame = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame",
  diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame + FS")

ptc_pos_ids <- ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE]

# 4-color palette: NMD/Control × PTC+/No PTC
pal4 <- c("NMD PTC+"    = "#d6604d",   # dark orange-red
          "NMD No PTC"  = "#fddbc7",   # light orange
          "Ctrl PTC+"   = "#4393c3",   # dark blue
          "Ctrl No PTC" = "#d1e5f0")   # light blue

stacked_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("c2", "c4"), function(comp) {
  key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
  fc <- set_results[[key]]$frame_comp
  if (is.null(fc)) return(NULL)
  ps <- fc$pair_summary
  # Denominator: coding pairs only (exclude non_coding and no_shared_cds)
  coding_pairs_total <- sum(!ps$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
  comp_lbl <- comp_label(comp)
  comp_short <- ifelse(comp_lbl == "NMD", "NMD", "Ctrl")

  do.call(rbind, lapply(coding_cats, function(cat) {
    cat_pairs <- ps[ps$frame_category == cat, ]
    n_cat <- nrow(cat_pairs)
    n_ptc <- sum(cat_pairs$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_pos_ids)
    n_no_ptc <- n_cat - n_ptc
    pct_ptc <- 100 * n_ptc / max(coding_pairs_total, 1)
    pct_no_ptc <- 100 * n_no_ptc / max(coding_pairs_total, 1)
    rbind(
      data.frame(frame_category = cat, category_label = cat_labels[cat],
                 comparison = comp_lbl, ptc_status = "PTC+",
                 fill_group = paste(comp_short, "PTC+"),
                 n = n_ptc, pct = pct_ptc),
      data.frame(frame_category = cat, category_label = cat_labels[cat],
                 comparison = comp_lbl, ptc_status = "No PTC",
                 fill_group = paste(comp_short, "No PTC"),
                 n = n_no_ptc, pct = pct_no_ptc))
  }))
}))

stacked_df$category_label <- factor(stacked_df$category_label,
  levels = cat_labels[coding_cats])
stacked_df$fill_group <- factor(stacked_df$fill_group,
  levels = c("NMD PTC+", "NMD No PTC", "Ctrl PTC+", "Ctrl No PTC"))

fig4 <- ggplot(stacked_df, aes(x = category_label, y = pct, fill = fill_group)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~comparison) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal4) +
  labs(title = "Frame Category Distribution: NMD vs Control (all_samples)",
       subtitle = "% of total pairs. PTC+ = comparator has premature termination codon.",
       x = "Frame Category", y = "% of Total Pairs", fill = "") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
save_fig(fig4, "fig5_frame_category_distribution", width = 10, height = 6)
```
